`TfidfVectorizer` builds sparse lexical features directly from supplied titles/descriptions, without pretrained weights. Its default tokenizer retains multi-character alphanumeric tokens but drops single-character tokens and splits punctuation—potentially damaging identifiers such as “AB-123,” decimals, and units. Suggested approach: a documented custom tokenizer preserving these forms, no numeric stripping, and conservative vocabulary pruning so rare model identifiers survive. Use L2 normalization and float32 storage; persist the vectorizer, item-row mapping, preprocessing settings, and library versions. [TfidfVectorizer documentation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.feature_extraction.text.TfidfVectorizer.html)

For retrieval, fit `NearestNeighbors(metric='cosine', algorithm='brute')` on sparse features and query in small batches, retaining only top-k results. Sparse input uses brute-force search; batching limits output memory but does not eliminate exhaustive comparison cost. Alternatively, compute sparse cosine products per query block with `dense_output=False`, remove self-matches, and immediately retain each row’s highest positive similarities. Sparse similarity output can still become large; use small blocks and avoid constructing the full item-by-item matrix. Explicitly handle empty documents, insufficient positive matches, and deterministic ties by item ID. [NearestNeighbors](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.neighbors.NearestNeighbors.html), [cosine_similarity](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.pairwise.cosine_similarity.html)

`pairwise_distances_chunked(metric='cosine', working_memory=..., reduce_func=...)` provides another bounded-memory route: reduce each distance block immediately to neighbor indices/distances. It avoids retaining the complete dense matrix, although individual blocks may be dense and total computation remains exhaustive. For this experiment, lexical neighbors can support training-time mining within the single HSTU model; they must not become an independently fitted inference score fused with neural predictions. [Chunked distances documentation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.pairwise_distances_chunked.html)
